LESSON: CAPACITY

Grade: PP2
Subject: MATHEMATICS ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.4: Capacity

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Capacity. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. compare sizes of containers using through filling and emptying using different substances and objects
2. appreciate the use of objects of different sizes in the environment
3. enjoy filling and emptying containers in the environment learners tell how much a container can hold compared to another one of a different size filling and emptying containers. comparing containers of different sizes.

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. compare sizes of containers using through filling and emptying using different substances and objects
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to compare sizes of containers using through filling and emptying using different substances and objects. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. appreciate the use of objects of different sizes in the environment
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to appreciate the use of objects of different sizes in the environment. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. enjoy filling and emptying containers in the environment learners tell how much a container can hold compared to another one of a different size filling and emptying containers. comparing containers of different sizes.
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to enjoy filling and emptying containers in the environment learners tell how much a container can hold compared to another one of a different size filling and emptying containers. comparing containers of different sizes. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market in your county, count 10 mangoes. Put them in 2 groups of 5. That is sorting and grouping.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row. Write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and your parent gives you 5 more, you have 12 shillings. That is addition.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Capacity.
2. Explain Capacity to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Try this activity: In groups or pairs, individually, learners tell how much a container can hold compared to another one of a different size
4. Show that you can: compare sizes of containers using through filling and emptying using different substances and objects
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Capacity. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Capacity important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. In groups or pairs, individually, learners tell how much a container can hold compared to another one of a different size
2. Watch a video on filling and emptying containers.
3. Food and nutrition: filling containers using different types of seeds and food staffs;

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. compare sizes of containers using through filling and emptying using different substances and objects
2. appreciate the use of objects of different sizes in the environment
3. enjoy filling and emptying containers in the environment learners tell how much a container can hold compared to another one of a different size filling and emptying containers. comparing containers of different sizes.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.
